This duality manifests as a fragmentation of belief systems, where each system caters to distinct cognitive needs—intellectual rigor versus affective resonance. The scientific conception gratification primitive underscores how materialistic models satisfy the former but neglect the latter. In contrast, the world-soul reactive phenomenon suggests a deeper causal structure underlying experience, implying that phenomena are not random but purposefully arranged to elicit specific cognitive responses. These primitives form a triadic structure: compromise as the operational mode, gratification as the evaluative criterion, and reactivity as the ontological foundation. Their interplay defines the epistemic boundary of belief systems, where failure modes emerge when one domain dominates at expense of others. The universal lens synthesizes these into a coherent framework for understanding how perception integrates multiple modalities into a unified yet fragmented worldview.
